summary: Independent QA of U2-b (SQL-only semantic persistence + transactional RPCs) on fresh lab root /tmp/voom-u2-replay-qa. All 7 requested test blocks (T1-T7) passed independently. T1 replay_up=REPLAY_UP DONE (pass1=67, policies=566) and replay_verify=checks=111 pass=111 fail=0. T2 run_u2b.sh printed 'U2B MIGRATION PASS 1 (idempotent)' + 'U2B MIGRATION PASS 2 (idempotent)' and ended with 'U2B DONE checks=98 pass=98 fail=0'; re-run same 98/98 (fully re-runnable); replay_verify after U2B still 111/111. T3 SQL spot-checks (a-e) all matched: (a) grants to non-owner on gptour_semantic_* tables = 0, (b) pg_policies on gptour_semantic_* = 0, (c) EXECUTE counts: authenticated=0, anon=0, service_role=0, gptour_semantic_backend=12, (d) role chain = 'gptour_semantic_backend->authenticator', (e) 'set role service_role; UPDATE gptour_semantic_sessions...' => 'ERROR: permission denied for table gptour_semantic_sessions' (table privilege, not trigger). T4 PostgREST unauth: GET /gptour_semantic_requests?select=* => 401 (as required). RPC with correct args (p_caller_uid,p_session_id,p_request_id,p_payload_hash,p_expected_revision) => 401 (as required); however the exact curl asked in the request body ('-d {}') returns 404 PGRST202 with message 'Could not find the function public.gptour_semantic_claim without parameters in the schema cache'. This is PostgREST overload-resolution behaviour, NOT an auth-posture issue (the RPC does require backend credential). Documented in test_criterion_notes below. T5 code review (read-only): no missing invariants found; every mutating RPC calls assert_backend + lock_session (which enforces ownership, is_authorized, and session expiry) + lock_fenced (ownership-via-session, pending-status, matching token, live lease, deadline). get_state/get_request/get_plan also enforce ownership+authz+expiry; get_plan additionally checks p.owner_uid==p_caller_uid. is_authorized includes Fase6 kill-switch (gptour_orchestrator_user_access.enabled). Grants are tight: 12 RPCs executable only by gptour_semantic_backend, is_authorized restricted to owner, tables fully revoked from public/anon/authenticated/service_role/backend. T6 regressions: SA=129, SC=43, SD=39, SE=21 all fail=0 (SEMANTIC SUITES DONE fail=0); U2 CONTRACT NODE+DENO DONE fail=0; git diff --exit-code 259ec92d --stat => empty; secret scan on u2b dir/results doc => no match. T7 cleanup: replay_down => 'REPLAY_DOWN DONE', /tmp/voom-u2-replay-qa removed; main-agent labs /tmp/voom-u2-replay and /tmp/voom-u2-lab untouched (still present, mtimes preserved).
action_items: None blocking. Consider the (minor) test-criterion observation in test_criterion_notes: an unauthenticated POST to /rpc/gptour_semantic_claim with empty body ({}) returns 404/PGRST202 (overload not found) rather than 401/403. With correct arguments the same unauthenticated POST returns 401, confirming security posture. If a public QA script wants to assert the auth posture at the RPC door, it should send the full argument list; alternatively, document the 404 outcome explicitly.

Verify_u2b.py disables and re-enables triggers (as gptour_semantic_owner) in B5/B7/B8 to simulate elapsed processing_deadline/response_expires_at/session 24h starvation. The intent is implied by context but is not commented in-source; consider adding a one-line comment at lines 221/270/280 of verify_u2b.py (not blocking).
critical_code_review_comments: 01_semantic_migration.sql line 164 (lock_session): uses a single 'not found' (PT404) for 3 distinct conditions (missing row, wrong owner, authorization revoked). This is intentional non-enumeration (also noted in verify B6 'not found non enumerante') and is a positive security property, not a bug.

01_semantic_migration.sql line 192 (claim): if the session is in-progress and now_ts >= response_expires_at while status='done', the function flips the request to 'expired' and nulls response_body (consistent with trigger invariant lines 94-95 'response cleared only at expiry tombstone'). Correct but subtle; verified by B7 of verify_u2b.py.

01_semantic_migration.sql line 287 (commit_success): fetches session without 'for update' and relies on lock_session (via lock_fenced -> lock_session on line 217) having already taken the session lock. Correct, but the comment should ideally say 'already locked by lock_fenced -> lock_session' for clarity; otherwise relies on implicit knowledge of the call chain.

01_semantic_migration.sql line 326 (release_recoverable): clamps p_retry_after_ms to >= 0 but does not enforce an upper bound. A malicious backend caller could set next_retry_at arbitrarily far in the future, effectively DoS'ing retries for this specific request. Low impact (requires compromised backend JWT) and self-contained to one request. Consider capping at e.g. processing_deadline or a small ceiling.

01_semantic_migration.sql line 383 (is_authorized grants): granted only to gptour_semantic_owner. Because the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs run as the owner, the nested call succeeds; direct invocation as backend is denied (confirmed by verify_u2b.py line 169-170). Good.

01_semantic_migration.sql line 130 (assert_backend): belt-and-braces check on BOTH claims->>'role' AND current_setting('role',true). This blocks a forged JWT with role='gptour_semantic_backend' submitted to a PostgREST that is anchored to a different authenticator schema; and conversely blocks a session that SET ROLE gptour_semantic_backend without JWT claims. Correct.

01_semantic_migration.sql line 108 (tg_plans): plans are strictly immutable on UPDATE but DELETE is handled separately by tg_no_delete (which allows only current_user='gptour_semantic_owner'). Combined effect: plans are append-only outside owner-run maintenance. Correct.

verify_u2b.py line 141-147 (B2): asserts that every RPC returns 401/403 for authenticated owner A, admin via user_metadata, service_role, anon, and backend-with-unknown-jti. Non-vacuous (ensures backend_keys gate works, no role-elevation path via user_metadata). Good.

verify_u2b.py line 221/270/280: disables triggers as gptour_semantic_owner to backdate processing_deadline/response_expires_at/created_at. The disable+re-enable is bracketed within the same statement block, but there is no 'begin/exception' guard: if the statement failed mid-way the trigger would remain disabled. Low risk for a one-shot QA script, but worth hardening with a transaction (begin; ... ; commit;) that re-enables in both branches, or using session_replication_role scoped to a transaction.

verify_u2b.py line 146 (B2 ok assertion): 'all(c in (401, 403) for c in codes.values())' — strict and non-vacuous. Note: anon RPC calls go through lib.http which sends no Authorization header; PostgREST returns 401 only when the RPC overload resolves. If any RPC signature changes without updating the args dict (lines 125-139), the call would 404 and the assertion would fail (good — not a vacuous-pass risk).
verify_u2b.py line 166 (B3): combined invariant 'DB invariato dopo i tentativi diretti' asserting rev=1, no rogue jti, 1 plan — specific values, not just 'no change'. Good.

success_rate.backend: 100% (U2B 98/98 x2, replay_verify 111/111 x2, SA/SC/SD/SE 129/43/39/21 fail=0, U2 CONTRACT NODE+DENO fail=0, all T3 SQL/T4 HTTP spot-checks matched)

test_credentials: N/A - local synthetic lab only. Synthetic HS256 JWTs built in-memory by replay_verify_lib.py/verify_u2b.py (backend jti='u2b-lab-key'). JWT secret file is 0600 and was NOT read; no token or secret printed in this report.
seed_data_creation: replay_up applied fixture.sql (synthetic agents A/B/C/D/E, 13 customers, zones). verify_u2b.py seeds 2 sessions and ~5 requests under test; all under /tmp/voom-u2-replay-qa which was removed in T7.
test_criterion_notes: T4 request-body expectation: 'curl -d {} /rpc/gptour_semantic_claim' must be 401/403. Observed 404 with PGRST202 'Could not find the function public.gptour_semantic_claim without parameters in the schema cache'. Reason: PostgREST overload resolution finds no RPC overload matching an empty body before authorization is evaluated. When the same POST is sent WITH the proper arg list (p_caller_uid,p_session_id,p_request_id,p_payload_hash,p_expected_revision) and no Authorization header, PostgREST returns 401 as expected (verified in-situ). The verify_u2b.py suite tests this correctly (B2) and passed 98/98; the auth posture is sound. The '-d {}' phrasing in the review request is unsatisfiable by construction with the real signature.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fresh-root reproducibility confirmed again on /tmp/voom-u2-replay-qa (~25s cold replay_up + ~5s U2B + ~15s verify_u2b.py). Required env: U2_PG_BIN=/usr/lib/postgresql/15/bin, U2_PG_OS_USER=postgres, U2_POSTGREST_BIN=/opt/voom-u2/bin/postgrest, U2_DENO_BIN=/opt/deno/deno, and a DEDICATED U2_REPLAY_ROOT (never /tmp/voom-u2-replay or /tmp/voom-u2-lab). PostgREST db-schemas='public', anon role, HS256 JWT secret in lab.json path (0600, do not read). For RPC HTTP checks always use the full argument signature or you will get 404/PGRST202 which is overload resolution, not auth. git diff vs 259ec92d must remain empty — do not edit anything under /app/voom-repo (only /app/test_reports). Main-agent labs preserved untouched.
rca of the issue: No functional issues. One test-criterion caveat for T4 (empty-body POST returns 404 due to PostgREST PGRST202 overload resolution, not an authz regression) and one minor code-quality nit on gptour_semantic_release_recoverable (no upper bound on p_retry_after_ms). Both non-blocking.
